title: Where else does mathematics help in daily life?
description: A market, a bus and a tiled floor each show a way that mathematics helps in everyday life. The video ends on the open discussion the book asks for.
teaching_notes: One idea: wherever we count, measure, travel or design, mathematics is at work. Any honest example from the child is welcome. Watch for students who think mathematics lives only in sums written in a notebook.

source: Figure it Out Q1 (Math Talk), p.2
video_script.why: The child names everyday places where mathematics helps, such as paying, travelling and designing, and sees it is not only for notebook sums.
video_script.substitution: Mathematics helps wherever we count, measure, travel or design.
video_script.anchor: a market, a bus and a tiled floor, the three places of an ordinary day
video_script.payoff_line: Mathematics helps whenever we count, measure, travel or design

final_answer.value: paying for fruits and vegetables; the speed of vehicles; tile designs and floor area
final_answer.spoken: paying for fruit and vegetables, the speed of a bus or train, and the designs and area of a floor

hold_back: Mathematics helps whenever we count, measure, travel or design
never_show: maths is only sums in a notebook
maths_rules: market: count the money and weigh the fruit and vegetables
bus or train: speed tells how long the trip takes
floor: tile designs repeat, and the area of the floor tells how many tiles are needed
open discussion: any honest example of counting, measuring, travelling or designing is acceptable
slip: sums in a notebook are only one small part of where mathematics is used
video_script.design: One idea: mathematics helps wherever we count, measure, travel or design. Callback to the earlier videos on patterns and reasons. Wrong idea: none is broken. The three places stay on the board to the end.
